title: No raise, but no pay cut
hook: Why might wage changes pile up at exactly zero?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Read a zero mass in a distribution without confusing nominal and real pay changes.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Read a zero mass in a distribution without confusing nominal and real pay changes.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy wage stays at €100 while prices rise 5%. In old-price euros, what purchasing power remains? Toy inputs A=[100, 5]; B=[95, 5].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[95.23809523809524, 100, 5], [90.47619047619047, 95, 5]]. Labels: Real wage €, Nominal €, Inflation %.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: A zero nominal wage change is different from a zero change in purchasing power. The comparison introduces an explicit nominal cut as well. Reading a spike at zero requires knowing which wage definition the distribution uses.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Nominal wage €=95, Inflation %=5. What is Real wage €? Answer: 90.476.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Nominal wage €=95, Inflation %=5. What is Real wage €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 90.476. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Wage-change data show a spike at exactly zero, since employers rarely cut nominal pay (Card & Hyslop, 1997; Kahn, 1997).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Read a zero mass in a distribution without confusing nominal and real pay changes.
